briefs.headline: Arsenal open the title defence 3-0 over Coventry
briefs.summary: Kai Havertz scored inside 15 minutes and Bukayo Saka doubled it before the break. Martin Odegaard added a third four minutes after halftime. Coventry are back after 25 years.

briefs.headline: Milwaukee hold the NL Central at 80-49
briefs.summary: The Brewers edged Atlanta 2-1 behind Misiorowski, now 13-5 with a 1.68 ERA. Houston shut out the Athletics 4-0 and Cleveland routed Colorado 9-1.

briefs.summary: The banzuke, the rankings sheet, is due Aug. 31. The Japan Sumo Association's English pages still carry no September schedule, only that every day is sold out.

sections.note: Sumo got its own search again. A Sept. 13-27 opening at Ryogoku Kokugikan is derived from the second-Sunday rule and is carried only by ticket resellers, travel sites and fan databases, which this paper does not cite - a ninth straight morning. sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 258 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Off 446 cfs a day ago and still dropping, so last week's storm water is nearly out. At this height it is still a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam problem rather than a long-leader one: a weighted stonefly or a sculpin along the undercut banks and the soft edges. Another day like this one puts it back near wading water.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.0 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Steady at pool for a second day, which keeps fish on structure. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and the riprap is the first look, and the lock wall holds fish now the colour has cleared.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 30.4 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Down a foot and a fifth on the day but still four and a half feet above the pool side of the dam, so it is high and coloured and debris is the hazard. The slack behind the rock and the wall is where to start, and a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap is the second look.

waters.reading: Sound highs 4:03 AM at 3.0 ft and 4:48 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 10:23 AM at 0.6 ft and 11:21 PM at 1.1 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:03 AM and 4:48 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure. The afternoon high is the bigger of the two at 3.9 feet and the only one in daylight, so the push into it and the first of the fall off it are the window. The moon is a waxing gibbous at 68% and nine days old, building toward spring tides, so the current through the inlet is stiffening rather than easing. Red drum want the last of that fall along the grass edges and the oyster bars; mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage. Flounder is catch-and-release until Sept. 1.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none for a sixth morning. The Fisherman's Post Topsail report is monthly and was published Aug. 3, 19 days old: it had red drum on topwater early and cut bait later, tarpon to an estimated 110 pounds and a 63-pound cobia off the end of Jolly Roger Pier, and speckled trout, pompano, sea mullet and spots from Surf City Pier. That is the month's pattern, not today's conditions. The National Weather Service at Wilmington carries no beach hazard, rip current or heat advisory for Pender County this morning.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: The Williams has come off 446 cfs to 258 in a day, and the Ohio below Byrd is down more than a foot.
